correctness.rationale: For every 0<c<=d<1 and 2c^2+d<1, the signed Gram matrix has eigenvalues 1+d and the eigenvalues of [[1,sqrt(2)c],[sqrt(2)c,1-d]], so it is SPD. Exact pair-block minimization leaves a rank-one H-orthogonal residual with Gram G. The maximum eigenvalue of a positive linear combination of three rank-one projections is convex in omission probabilities and invariant under leaf exchange. Symmetrization reduces minimax to p=(a,(1-a)/2,(1-a)/2). The antisymmetric leaf eigenvalue decreases linearly; the larger symmetric-block eigenvalue crosses it uniquely at a=d(1+d)/(2c^2+d^2+3d) and is strictly increasing thereafter by its positive derivative and convexity. Uniform volume sampling follows from equal inverse-Hessian diagonals; the exact strict gap and limiting ratio are analytic identities. The packaged script confirms the algebra and samples 193536 finite cases, without claiming finite testing proves the continuum.

value.rationale: The family has a natural antagonistic two-leaf correlation and positively coupled hub; it lies outside the signable regime where existing optimal-sampling formulas are available. In this family volume sampling uses uniformly distributed omission despite nonuniform worst-case error geometry. The full c<=d SPD regime has an explicit globally optimal law, a strict equality boundary at c=d and a sharp 4/3 asymptotic retention gap (3/2 for guaranteed decrement). This is a substantive quantitative sampling-design limitation rather than a single arbitrary parameter example. It makes no claim about multi-step or runtime gains.
